Considerations for selection of measures depend on the resources available to the research team as well as parental preferences
and concerns; however, the method(s) need to be sufﬁciently sensitive to detect small differences in FM and FFM between the inter-
vention group and usual care group. In most studies, length and weight were most commonly measured because they are the least
intrusive; generally require little skill, training, and equipment; and can be conducted quickly with minimal costs. However, length
